message.content: {"caption":"Three-panel schematic of memory creation through unaggregated, parallel, and sequential reasoning trajectories.","description":"The diagram compares three left-to-right processes, each running from Task q_i to Task q_{i+1}. In (a), “Vanilla TTS (MaTTS w/o aggregation),” rows pair memory items “Mem 1,” “Mem 2,” …, “Mem n” with “Traj 1,” “Traj 2,” …, “Traj n,” then with corresponding “New Mem 1,” “New Mem 2,” …, “New Mem n.” Arrows point from each memory item to its trajectory and onward to its new-memory item. The document icons represent stored memory and the document-and-lightbulb icons represent newly created memory; dotted rows indicate omitted intermediate items. In (b), “MaTTS - Parallel,” a “Current memory” box, illustrated with a memory document and an agent icon, branches via arrows to a dashed group of parallel trajectories: “Trajectory 1,” “Trajectory 2,” and “Trajectory n.” Trajectory 1 and Trajectory n have green check marks; Trajectory 2 has a red cross. Small note-like comparison symbols sit beside the trajectory group, followed by a right-pointing blue arrow labeled “Self-Contrast” that leads to “New memory,” shown with a document-and-lightbulb icon and agent icon. In (c), “MaTTS - Sequential,” an arrow leads from a similar “Current memory” box to a dashed “Self-Refine” group containing “Traj,” “Traj′,” and an ellipsis. Red crossed-out editing symbols and curved red arrows indicate successive refinement steps. A right-pointing blue arrow leads from this group to “New memory.” The agent and memory-document icons recur in the memory boxes; the lightbulb marks newly formed memory.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
